**Finding: deviation (EXCLUSIVITY, high)** — Section 6.1 (p0037).

- **What binds us:** The Company may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products "during the term of this Agreement," and HDI takes the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site. The only carve-out (6.2) is closeout merchandise.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** The term auto-renews annually under Section 4.1, so the exclusivity is open-ended, and nothing ends it if HDI underperforms — Section 1.6 covers only a missed initial launch, and Company termination under Section 4.2 carries a Termination Payment. That is exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit (walk-away territory).
- **Not flagged:** Section 6.3 (HDI restrained for the term plus two years) benefits us and is left intact.
- **Redline (validated, fallback level):** cap the exclusivity at twelve months from the Effective Date and add automatic, penalty-free termination of the exclusivity on HDI's launch or service/availability/delivery failures uncured after ten days' notice. Fallback rather than outright deletion is proportionate given the reciprocal restraint in 6.3 and the revenue-share bargain.
